verdict.rationale: OpenRouter's docs let users restrict routing to providers with a certain data policy and set an account-wide toggle to disallow routing to providers that may train on user data, directly enabling the story's goal (docs-12, docs-25, docs-33). However, this relies on providers' self-reported policies rather than a first-party guarantee, and community commentary questions the strength of these privacy assurances ('no true guarantees of ZDR/privacy/data sovereignty', 'No ZDR. No dice.'), suggesting real-world confidence in strict enforcement is limited. Missing for 10: independent verification that opted-out providers never train on data, and clearer enforcement/audit mechanisms beyond self-attested provider policy.
